title: House Construction Contract in Vietnam 2026: Required Content
desc: What a house construction contract should contain under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 210/2026/ND-CP: scope, price, schedule, acceptance, warranty.
summary: The content a homeowner should include in a house construction contract under Article 82 of the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 210/2026/ND-CP, with commonly missed points.
body: p

From 1 July 2026, construction contracts follow Construction Law No. 135/2025/QH15 and Decree 210/2026/ND-CP (replacing Decree 37/2015/ND-CP). A contract between a homeowner and a building contractor is a construction contract, so it must be made in writing and also comply with civil law (Article 80).
h2
1. What kind of contract is a house construction contract?
p

Under Article 6 of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP, a construction contract is a contract to build a work, work item or part of the work according to the design. If the contractor both designs and builds, it is a design-build contract (EC). The construction scope may include supplying supplies and materials, installing equipment, and quality testing (Point b, Clause 2, Article 8).
h2
2. Content the contract should include
p
Under Clause 4, Article 82 of the Construction Law 2025, depending on the scale of work, a construction contract may include:
ol
Legal basis; applicable law and language (Vietnamese).
Content and quantity of work.
Requirements on quality, technical standards, acceptance and handover.
Time and schedule of performance.
Contract price, advance payment, payment, final settlement, payment currency and contract liquidation.
Performance security for the parties' obligations.
Contract amendments; rights and obligations of the parties.
Liability for breach, rewards and penalties for breach.
Suspension and termination of the contract; dispute resolution.
Risks, force majeure events and fundamental change of circumstances.
p
The party information section states clearly the name, representative, address, tax code, account number, telephone, and the time and place of signing (Clause 2, Article 7).
h2
3. Points homeowners often miss
ul
Quantity and drawings: state clearly which design documents the contractor builds to, who supplies the materials, and the type and origin (Article 8; Clause 1, Article 9).

Acceptance: agree which work must be accepted before continuing (foundation, reinforcement, etc.) and who signs the record. For defective work, the party that caused the defect bears all costs of remedying it (Clause 2, Article 9).
Schedule: the contractor prepares a schedule for the homeowner's approval, with completion milestones for each part (Article 10).
What the price includes: state which costs, taxes and fees are and are not included in the price (Clause 2, Article 11).
Warranty: conditions, period and level of warranty security; if the contractor fails to perform the warranty, the homeowner may use the security to hire another party (Clause 2, Article 20).
All requests and proposals in writing (including text messages and emails under electronic transaction law) and sent to the address stated in the contract (Clause 4, Article 4).
h2
4. Contract documents and order of priority
p

The contract documents consist of the contract, appendices and accompanying documents. When the documents conflict and the parties have not agreed on an order of priority, Clause 5, Article 82 applies: the contract agreement, particular conditions, general conditions, then design drawings, technical instructions, negotiation records, appendices, etc. So anything important should be written directly into the contract and not left only in a quotation.
h2
5. When does the contract take effect?
p

A contract takes effect when it meets the conditions for validity of a civil transaction and the parties have the conditions and capacity required by the Construction Law; the effective time is the time of signing or another time agreed by the parties (Article 81). A main contractor may subcontract only to parties with the right capacity and remains responsible to the homeowner for the subcontractor's schedule and quality (Article 19).
p
Before construction, see also Conditions to start building a house 2026.
note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace the legal documents. Many detailed provisions of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP are mandatory only for public investment and PPP projects; for private houses, most content is agreed by the two parties. Contracts signed before 1 July 2026 are performed under the Construction Law 2014 (Clause 7, Article 95 of the Construction Law 2025).
